en.name: Alphonsa of India
en.summary: The first woman of Indian origin canonized a saint, a Franciscan Clarist nun known for embracing a lifetime of suffering.
en.body: Born Anna Muttathupadathu in Kudamaloor, Kerala, in 1910, Alphonsa entered the Franciscan Clarist Congregation and took the religious name Alphonsa in honor of Alphonsus Liguori. She endured chronic and often severe illness for most of her religious life, including a mysterious ailment that left her bedridden for her final years, which she came to understand as a form of redemptive suffering offered for others. She died in 1946 at the convent in Bharananganam, Kerala, still in her thirties. Devotion to her grew rapidly among the faithful in Kerala after her death, and she was canonized by Pope Benedict XVI in 2008, becoming the first woman of Indian origin to be declared a saint by the Catholic Church.
